name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks into a local folder for direct inspection—`mkdir eitan-picks && cd eitan-picks`, then `wget -r -l 2 -nd -H -A png,jpg,jpeg,svg https://mineai.com/eitan/picks/` to grab all images (max 2 deep, no dirs, only common image types). I’ll then run `exiftool -csv -r -ext png -ext jpg -ext svg -ext jpeg . > picks-meta.csv` to log dimensions, color profiles, and creation dates for taste-learning. Next, I’ll open the folder in VS Code and create a quick `index.html` with a grid of thumbnails for side-by-side comparison.

name: Squint
text: Squint here—your `wget` command’s `-H` flag risks crawling *off-site* domains if Eitan’s picks link externally, bloating the folder with unrelated assets. Where’s the `-D mineai.com` restriction to lock scope? Also, `exiftool` output isn’t a design artifact—it’s metadata. The *real* deliverable should be a curated visual board (e.g., Figma/PDF) with annotated picks, not raw files. Show me the filtering logic or I call foul.
